questions.stem: A regional bank servicing its Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) is an example of what type of field service?
questions.explanation: A bank servicing its own ATMs at external customer locations is external field service. External field service involves technicians traveling to locations outside the organization's premises to service equipment. Reactive field service responds to breakdowns; internal field service covers in-house maintenance; predictive field service uses sensor data to anticipate failures.

questions.stem: What field service model is used for maintenance at regular intervals?
questions.explanation: Planned (preventive) maintenance is performed at regular scheduled intervals regardless of equipment condition. This contrasts with predictive maintenance (based on data/sensor analysis), reactive maintenance (responding to breakdowns), and project-based maintenance (one-off initiatives). Planned maintenance follows a fixed schedule such as quarterly or monthly.

questions.stem: What state must a work order request be in to set dependencies for work order tasks?
questions.explanation: The work order must be in Draft state to set dependencies between its work order tasks. Dependencies are configured during work order setup before the order is promoted through the qualification process. Once the work order advances beyond draft, dependency configuration is locked.

questions.stem: What do administrators use to create questionnaires for work orders and work order tasks?
questions.explanation: Assessment Designer is the ServiceNow platform tool used to create questionnaires for work orders and work order tasks. Assessment Designer allows admins to build custom questionnaire templates with different question types that can be attached to FSM records. Process Automation Designer is for workflows, Survey Designer is a different tool, and Targeted Communication is for notifications.

questions.stem: When can work order tasks be dispatched?
questions.explanation: Work order tasks can be dispatched once a dispatch group is assigned to the task. The dispatch group determines which dispatchers can manage and assign the task. Without a dispatch group, the task cannot enter the dispatch workflow. Parts sourcing, agent assignment, and appointment booking occur after or during the dispatch process.

questions.stem: Dispatcher workspace looks at which calendar to auto-assign tasks to agents based on availability?
questions.explanation: Dispatcher workspace checks the Agent calendar to determine agent availability when auto-assigning tasks. The agent calendar contains work schedules, personal time off, shift information, and blocked time. The system evaluates agent calendars to find available time slots that match task requirements.

questions.stem: Which operational role typically creates personal events for an agent's calendar?
questions.explanation: The wm_dispatcher role typically creates personal events on an agent's calendar in the Dispatcher Workspace. Dispatchers manage agent schedules and create events to block time for appointments, meetings, training, or unavailability. While agents (wm_agent) can see their calendars, dispatchers are the operational role that manages personal event creation.

questions.stem: How are dispatch groups that can be selected from work order tasks filtered?
questions.explanation: Dispatch groups available on work order tasks are filtered by location coverage. Each dispatch group defines the geographic areas it covers, and only groups whose coverage area includes the task's location are shown as options on the work order task form. This ensures tasks are routed to dispatchers responsible for that area.

questions.stem: Where can dispatchers view real-time locations of agents?
questions.explanation: The Dispatch Map in Dispatcher Workspace shows real-time locations of field agents on an interactive map. This allows dispatchers to see where agents currently are, track their movements, and make informed assignment decisions based on agent proximity to tasks. The Agent map is for agents, not dispatchers.

questions.stem: When using territory management, what can field service admins assign to an individual or group?
questions.explanation: Territory management allows field service admins to assign locations (geographic territories/coverage areas) to individual agents or groups. Territories define which agents can be assigned tasks in specific regions. Skills are managed separately via skills management, and parts/routes are not directly assigned through territory management.

questions.stem: When using the dispatcher workspace integration with dynamic scheduling, if a dispatcher drags a lower priority task over a higher priority task, what will occur?

options.text: A warning is displayed and dispatcher confirmation is required
The higher priority task is automatically reassigned

questions.explanation: When a dispatcher drags a lower priority task over a higher priority task in the dispatcher workspace with dynamic scheduling, a warning is displayed and dispatcher confirmation is required. This safeguard prevents accidental priority overrides. The system alerts the dispatcher that the action may delay a higher-priority task and requires explicit confirmation before proceeding.

questions.stem: What state do work order tasks need to be in for dynamic scheduling to assign them?
questions.explanation: Work order tasks must be in 'Pending dispatch' state for dynamic scheduling to assign them. This state indicates the task has been qualified and is ready for scheduling but hasn't been assigned to an agent yet. Dynamic scheduling picks up tasks in Pending dispatch state and automatically assigns them based on agent availability, location, skills, and other matching criteria.

questions.stem: In the context of time recording, “Out of office”, “Meeting”, and “Training” are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Out of office, Meeting, and Training are examples of time worked categories in FSM time recording. Time worked categories classify different types of time entries agents can log, including productive work time and non-productive time like meetings or training. Labor rate cards define billing rates, time sheet policies govern recording rules, and rate types categorize billing.

questions.stem: What allows for more accurately tracking agent’s locations through mobile devices?
questions.explanation: Geolocation allows for more accurately tracking agents' locations through mobile devices. FSM uses the mobile device's GPS capabilities to track field agent positions in real-time, enabling accurate travel time estimates, proximity-based task assignment, and live map views in the dispatcher workspace showing current agent locations relative to task sites.

questions.stem: What feature reorders an agent’s tasks for the day as efficiently as possible, using either geolocation or straight-line estimation?
questions.explanation: Route Optimization reorders an agent's tasks for the day to minimize travel time using either geolocation (Google Maps API for real-time travel estimates) or straight-line estimation. Dynamic Scheduling assigns tasks to agents but does not reorder existing task sequences. Dispatch Workflow manages the dispatch process, and Appointment Booking handles customer scheduling.

questions.stem: What does it mean when you set a work order task as an upstream task?

options.text: The downstream task must he approved before completing an upstream task
The task must he completed before any downstream tasks can be started
The task is dependent on another work order request
The task cannot he started until any upstream tasks have been completed

questions.explanation: Setting a work order task as an upstream task means it must be completed before any downstream (successor) tasks can be started. This creates a Finish-to-Start dependency where the downstream task waits until the upstream task is done. Dynamic scheduling only supports Finish-to-Start dependencies with no max/min lag time.

questions.stem: What sets and enforces the order in which a single field agent or multiple field agents perform the tasks assigned to them?
questions.explanation: Work Order Dependencies set and enforce the order in which field agents perform tasks. Dependencies define upstream/downstream relationships between tasks, creating Finish-to-Start chains. Task dependencies override task ordering rules to ensure proper task flow. Work Order Qualification is a state, circular relationships are invalid, and templates organize but don't enforce order.

questions.stem: Reactive, Planned, and Predictive are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Reactive, Planned, and Predictive are examples of field service models. These represent different maturity levels: Reactive (break-fix, respond as issues occur), Planned (scheduled maintenance, preventive work), and Predictive (using data/IoT to anticipate failures). Organizations progress through these models as FSM maturity increases, moving from firefighting to proactive service delivery.

questions.stem: Which reasons can field agents provide when rejecting tasks that were assigned to them? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Standard FSM task rejection reasons for field agents are: Type of work not preferred (B), Parts unavailable (C), Customer unavailable (D), and Schedule conflict (F). "Not a preferred customer" (A) is not a standard rejection reason in FSM. Skills mismatch (E) is handled during the dynamic scheduling matching phase before assignment, not as a post-assignment rejection reason.

questions.stem: What can customer service agents use to create and view associated work order tasks for customer cases?
questions.explanation: Customer service agents use Agent Workspace to create and view associated work order tasks for customer cases. The CSM Agent Workspace provides a unified interface where agents can manage cases and directly create field service work orders linked to those cases, view existing work order tasks, and track their progress without switching applications.

questions.stem: What can field agents use to record time spent on tasks on a day-to-day basis and submit the time sheet in a single action?
questions.explanation: Field agents can use the Time sheet portal to record time spent on tasks on a day-to-day basis and submit the time sheet in a single action. This portal provides a streamlined interface for logging hours against specific work order tasks and submitting completed time sheets, simplifying the time tracking and approval process for field service operations.

questions.stem: Field Service Management (FSM) is a solution for anything that uses which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Field Service Management is a solution for anything that uses Skills, Locations, and Time. These three elements are fundamental to FSM: Skills define agent capabilities needed for tasks, Locations determine where work must be performed and enable proximity-based routing, and Time governs scheduling, SLA management, and agent availability. Problems, Requests, and Incidents are ITSM concepts, not FSM core elements.

questions.stem: Location, skills, and availability are used to determine what?

options.text: The best field agent for a task

questions.explanation: Location, skills, and availability are used to determine the best field agent for a task. Dynamic scheduling evaluates these three criteria to optimally match tasks to agents: the agent must have the required skills, be available during the needed timeframe, and be within reasonable travel distance. This ensures efficient resource utilization and timely service delivery.

questions.stem: What phase in the baseline ServiceNow field service management process lifecycle immediately precedes the scheduling and dispatch phase?
questions.explanation: The FSM process lifecycle follows: Initiation > Qualification > Scheduling & Dispatch > Delivery & Confirmation > Analyze & Improve. Qualification immediately precedes the scheduling and dispatch phase. During qualification, the work order is reviewed, tasks are created, and the work is prepared for dispatch.

questions.stem: What determines if a rejected task is dynamically assigned to the same agent in the next 24 hours or not?
questions.explanation: The system property work.management.rejected.technician.duration determines whether a rejected task is dynamically assigned to the same agent within the next 24 hours. The "Ignore Rejected Technician" matching criterion in dynamic scheduling reads this property to enforce the exclusion period. Unassignment constraints serve a different purpose (preventing task unassignment).

questions.stem: Configuring SMS notifications to customers that include an agent's current location and estimated time of arrival depends on which plugins? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: SMS notifications with agent location and ETA to customers require two plugins: Notify - Twilio Direct Driver (A) provides the SMS delivery capability via Twilio, and Field Service Management - Customer Experience (D) provides customer-facing location tracking and ETA functionality. Push Notifications (C) handles push not SMS, and Notification Preferences (B) manages preferences, not delivery.

questions.stem: When sourcing a part, the From Stockroom field is auto-populated with a default stockroom location, only if: (Choose three.)

options.text: The parts scheduling plugin is activated
The Reserve parts in agent stockroom configuration option is enabled
The field agent has preferred stockrooms defined
The part is available in the agent’s personal stockroom
The part is available in the assignment group’s stockroom

questions.explanation: The From Stockroom field auto-populates with a default stockroom only if all three conditions are met: the parts scheduling plugin is activated (A) enabling the feature, the "Reserve parts in agent stockroom" configuration option is enabled (B), and the required part is available in the agent's personal stockroom (D). Without any of these conditions, auto-population does not occur.

questions.stem: Map page markers, map filters, and map data are key components of what?
questions.explanation: Map page markers, map filters, and map data are key components of the Dispatcher Workspace. The dispatch map within the workspace uses markers to show agent and task locations, filters to refine the map view, and map data sources to populate location information. Territory Management uses territories, and Geolocation is a capability, not a UI component.

questions.stem: Where can dispatchers view the location history of field agents to track and review their activities over a historical period?
questions.explanation: The Dispatch Map provides location history functionality for field agents, allowing dispatchers to track and review agent activities over a historical period. While Agent Location History Map (A) sounds plausible, the standard FSM feature for viewing agent location history is within the Dispatch Map in Dispatcher Workspace.

questions.stem: Which reasons can field agents provide when rejecting tasks that were assigned to them? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When rejecting assigned tasks, field agents can provide two reasons: (B) Skills mismatch — the agent doesn't have the required skills for the task, and (D) Parts unavailable — necessary parts or equipment aren't available. These are legitimate operational reasons. 'Type of work not preferred' (A) and 'Not a preferred customer' (C) are subjective preferences, not valid business reasons for rejection.

questions.stem: What is used to organize work into tasks and can also be published in the service catalog as catalog items?
questions.explanation: Work order templates organize work into predefined tasks and can be published as catalog items in the service catalog. This enables end users to create work orders with pre-configured task structures through self-service. Appointment booking, dynamic scheduling, and SLAs serve different purposes and cannot be published as catalog items.

questions.stem: What can be used to separate field service management data, processes, and administrative tasks into logical groupings called domains?
questions.explanation: Domain separation is used to separate field service management data, processes, and administrative tasks into logical groupings called domains. This ServiceNow platform feature enables multi-tenant configurations where different business units or regions can have isolated FSM data and processes within a single instance while sharing the same infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow integrations for Field Service Management (FSM) are available? (Choose two.)

options.text: FSM integration with Project Portfolio Management (PPM)

questions.explanation: Available FSM integrations include Asset Management integration (C) and Customer Service Management (CSM) integration (E). Asset Management integration enables tracking of parts, assets, and inventory for field service tasks. CSM integration allows customer service agents to create work orders from cases. PPM integration (A), standalone Work Order Management (B), and Outlook Calendar (D) are not standard OOB FSM integrations.

questions.stem: What needs to be enabled in the field service configuration order to allow customers to digitally sign and confirm work orders?

options.text: Work notes are required to close a task
Signature Capture and PDF Order Summary
Copy task work notes to request

questions.explanation: Signature Capture and PDF Order Summary must be enabled in the field service configuration to allow customers to digitally sign and confirm work orders. This feature enables field agents to collect customer signatures on mobile devices and generate a PDF summary of the completed work order for customer records and proof of service delivery.

questions.stem: Enabling the Use dispatch queue option in the field service assignment configuration allows dispatchers to?

options.text: Use the dispatch queue for manual assignment of tasks
Assign tasks based on assignment group coverage areas
Auto-select agents for tasks based on skill

questions.explanation: Enabling the Use dispatch queue option in the field service assignment configuration allows dispatchers to use the dispatch queue for manual assignment of tasks. Tasks enter the dispatch queue where dispatchers can review and manually assign them to appropriate agents rather than relying on automatic assignment methods.

questions.stem: What is used to categorize different types of work for time reporting?
questions.explanation: Rate Models categorize different types of work for time reporting in FSM. Rate models group rate types and rate lines into organized structures that define how time entries are classified, billable versus non-billable, and at what rates. Time Cards are individual time entries, Rate Types classify rate categories, and Rate Lines are specific rate values.

questions.stem: What is used to estimate distance and time to determine the best route for an agent if Google Maps API is not configured?
questions.explanation: When Google Maps API is not configured, straight line estimates (Haversine distance) are used to estimate distance and time for determining the best route for an agent. This calculates the direct geographic distance between two points using latitude/longitude coordinates. While less accurate than actual road routing, it provides a reasonable approximation for scheduling decisions.

questions.stem: What happens to a task that cannot be auto-assigned because of an impractical or missing location or because the task window cannot be scheduled?

options.text: Constraints are overridden and the task is assigned
The task is returned to the pending dispatch state
The task is set to the unassigned state
Constraints are presented to dispatcher for override confirmation

questions.explanation: When a task cannot be auto-assigned because of an impractical location, missing location, or an unschedulable time window, it is returned to the pending dispatch state. This allows dispatchers to manually review and handle the task. The system does not override constraints, set to unassigned, or prompt for confirmation in this scenario.

questions.stem: Transfer order line tasks are used to move which type of record through the asset shipment and drop-off transfer process?
questions.explanation: Transfer order line tasks are used to move Transfer order line records through the asset shipment and drop-off transfer process. Transfer order lines represent individual items being transferred between stockrooms. The line tasks track the shipping and receiving steps for each line item, managing the logistics of moving parts and assets to where field agents need them.

questions.stem: Which mobile application does field service use?
questions.explanation: Field Service Management uses the Mobile Agent application. Mobile Agent is a native mobile app providing field agents an intuitive interface to view assigned tasks, record time, manage parts, capture signatures, and work online or offline. Now Mobile is a general-purpose mobile app, Mobile Studio is for app development, and Mobile Onboarding is for HR.

questions.stem: What assignment method uses this calculation for task assignment '(Criteria_1 rating x Criteria_1 weight) / total criterion weight + (Critena_2 rating x Critena_2 weight) / total criterion weight + (Critena_3 rating x Criteria_3 weight) / total of criterion weight'?
questions.explanation: This formula is the Dynamic Scheduling agent ranking calculation. Dynamic scheduling multiplies each criterion's rating by its weight, divides by the total weight of all criteria, and sums the results to produce an agent score. Agents are ranked by this score, with the highest score earning the highest ranking for task assignment.

questions.stem: Each matching criteria defined in the dynamic scheduling configuration task filter is assigned a default weight of?
questions.explanation: Each matching criteria defined in the dynamic scheduling configuration task filter is assigned a default weight of 10. This default weight provides equal importance to all matching criteria initially. Administrators can adjust individual weights to prioritize certain criteria (like skills match or proximity) over others when the dynamic scheduling engine evaluates and ranks potential agents for a task.

questions.stem: When a dynamic scheduling task filter's auto assignment frequency is set to immediate, what happens?

options.text: Tasks are auto-assigned as soon as they are ready to be assigned
Tasks which are ready to be assigned are selected at the defined interval and assigned
Tasks are auto-assigned as soon as they reach the qualified state
Tasks are added to a batch and auto assigned at the defined interval

questions.explanation: When a task filter's auto assignment frequency is set to Immediate, tasks are auto-assigned as soon as they are ready to be assigned. This contrasts with Interval mode where tasks are batched and assigned at defined time intervals. The Immediate setting triggers Dynamic Scheduling instantly when a task meets the filter conditions.

questions.stem: Task filters, task ordering rules, and un-assignment constraints are key components of which feature?
questions.explanation: Task filters, task ordering rules, and un-assignment constraints are key components of Dynamic Scheduling. Dynamic scheduling uses these three components together: task filters define which tasks to process and matching criteria, task ordering rules determine the sequence in which tasks are scheduled, and un-assignment constraints define conditions under which already-assigned tasks can be reassigned.

questions.stem: As it pertains to time recording, FSM Rate Card Task Work (Billable) and FSM Rate Card Task Work OT (Billable), are examples of what?
questions.explanation: "FSM Rate Card Task Work (Billable)" and "FSM Rate Card Task Work OT (Billable)" are examples of labor rate cards. Labor rate cards define billing rates for different categories of field service work including standard task work and overtime (OT) work. Rate types classify categories, time cards are individual entries, and time worked is logged hours.

questions.stem: When defining a maintenance schedule, what type of trigger would you use for work to be performed based on time and count?
questions.explanation: When defining a maintenance schedule where work is performed based on both time and count, use the "Duration or Meter" trigger type. Duration handles time-based intervals (e.g., every 6 months) and Meter handles count-based intervals (e.g., every 1000 units). The "or" means either threshold triggers the maintenance work order.

questions.stem: As it pertains to time recording, what allows field agents to record beyond the standard 40 hours of time per week?

options.text: Configure time sheet notifications for manager override
Create a new time sheet policy for the specified field agents
Configure the time sheet portal widget
Activate the FSM with Time Recording plugin

questions.explanation: To allow field agents to record time beyond the standard 40 hours per week, create a new time sheet policy with a higher maximum weekly hours limit. Time sheet policies define rules for time recording including max hours. Activating the plugin (D) enables the feature but doesn't change the hour limit. Notifications (A) and portal widgets (C) don't affect hour limits.

questions.stem: Where can you disable the accept or reject task option if business process dictates that field agents should not have the ability to accept or reject tasks?
questions.explanation: The accept or reject task option can be disabled in the Field Service Configuration Business Process settings. This configuration controls the business process lifecycle for work order tasks, including whether field agents have the ability to accept or reject assigned tasks. When disabled, tasks are directly assigned without requiring agent acceptance.

questions.stem: In the Auto-Assignment Confirmation pop up window, what is the category of a previously assigned task which was unassigned, but, then, could not be assigned to any agent?
questions.explanation: In the Auto-Assignment Confirmation popup, a previously assigned task that was unassigned by dynamic scheduling but then could not be assigned to any other agent is categorized as "Not Assigned." This indicates the system attempted reassignment but no suitable agent was found, leaving the task in an unassigned state requiring manual intervention.

questions.stem: Which operational role is responsible for performing work onsite and reporting status?
questions.explanation: The wm_agent (field agent) operational role is responsible for performing work onsite and reporting status. Field agents are the front-line workers who travel to customer locations, execute the work described in work order tasks, and update task status upon completion. The manager (A) oversees operations, qualifier (B) manages qualifications, and dispatcher (C) handles scheduling.

questions.stem: When using mandatory skills and dynamic scheduling, which matching criteria should be configured in the dynamic scheduling task filter?

options.text: Matching Mandatory Skills for Dynamic Scheduling
Matching Skills Level Gap for Dynamic Scheduling

questions.explanation: "Matching Mandatory Skills For Dynamic Scheduling" is the matching criterion to configure when using mandatory skills with dynamic scheduling. This criterion ranks agents based on mandatory and optional skills defined in Task Skills. It evaluates whether agents possess the required mandatory skills for the task. The Matching Skills - Mandatory Skills Support criterion applies to CSM cases, not FSM tasks.

questions.stem: What criteria are utilized in auto-assignment of work order tasks? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Auto-assignment of work order tasks utilizes three criteria: (C) Skills — matching agent capabilities to task requirements, (D) Task windows — ensuring the task falls within allowable scheduling windows, and (E) Geolocation — considering agent proximity to the task location. SLA status (A) and age of task (B) are not primary criteria used by the auto-assignment algorithm.

questions.stem: Which operational rote can view the calendars of team members to check availability, view the skid distribution, and create or edit skills of team members?
questions.explanation: The wm_qualifier operational role can view calendars of team members to check availability, view skill distribution, and create or edit skills of team members. The qualifier is responsible for managing field agent qualifications and skills, ensuring agents are properly certified and skilled for their assigned work. This includes maintaining the skills database and verifying agent capabilities.

questions.stem: As it pertains to dynamic scheduling configuration, matching criteria, weighting, and ranking method are components of what?
questions.explanation: In dynamic scheduling configuration, matching criteria, weighting, and ranking method are components of Task Filters. Task filters define how the dynamic scheduling engine evaluates and ranks potential agents: matching criteria specify what agent attributes to evaluate, weighting determines the relative importance of each criterion, and the ranking method defines how agents are scored and ordered.

questions.stem: Assuming the reserve parts in agent stockroom configuration option is enabled, when sourcing a part, the From Stockroom field is auto-populated with a default stockroom location, only if:

options.text: The parts scheduling plugin is activated
The part is available in the dispatcher’s stockroom
The part is available in the agent’s personal stockroom
The field agent has preferred stockrooms defined

questions.explanation: When the reserve parts in agent stockroom option is enabled, the From Stockroom field auto-populates with a default stockroom location only if the part is available in the agent's personal stockroom. The system checks the assigned agent's personal stockroom first. If the part exists there, it's automatically selected as the source, streamlining the parts sourcing process.

questions.stem: What determines which tasks appear on the task panel in dispatcher workspace?
questions.explanation: Task Panel Filters determine which tasks appear on the task panel in the Dispatcher Workspace. Dispatchers configure these filters to display specific subsets of tasks based on criteria like state, priority, assignment group, or other task attributes. Task Panel Sorting controls order, Card Fields controls data displayed, and Dispatcher filters is not a specific feature.

questions.stem: What feature helps field agents by providing relevant knowledge for the task at hand and displaying search results on forms when users enter text in a field?
questions.explanation: Contextual search helps field agents by providing relevant knowledge for the task at hand and displaying search results on forms when users enter text in a field. As agents type in fields like short description or work notes, contextual search automatically queries the knowledge base and displays related articles, helping agents find solutions, procedures, and reference material without leaving the form.

questions.stem: What can be used to send articles, notices, and announcements to relevant customers?
questions.explanation: Targeted communication is used to send articles, notices, and announcements to relevant customers. This FSM feature enables proactive customer communication by allowing organizations to publish targeted messages to specific customer segments through the service portal. Unlike generic email notifications (A) or portal notifications (B), targeted communication delivers curated content to specific audiences.

questions.stem: When configuring an appointment booking record producer, what must be enabled in order to display the appointment selection widget on the record producer?
questions.explanation: The appointment booking variable set must be enabled and added to the record producer to display the appointment selection widget. Variable sets bundle form fields together, and the appointment booking variable set specifically contains the appointment scheduling UI elements. Work order templates and catalog definitions serve different purposes.

questions.stem: When you book an appointment, the timezone of appointment slots will be displayed based on? (Choose two.)

options.text: The location where the appointment for the task is scheduled
Timezone that is specified m the user contact record
The Timezone of the available agent
The location of the available agent

questions.explanation: When booking an appointment, the timezone of displayed appointment slots is based on: the location where the appointment for the task is scheduled (A) which provides the service area timezone, and the timezone specified in the user contact record (B) which determines the end user's preferred timezone for display. Agent timezone and location are considered for availability, not slot display.

questions.stem: If you are using auto-routing or auto-dispatch, what must be set in system properties for precise time estimates?

options.text: Latitude and longtitude for Google Maps API
Private Key and Client ID for Google Maps API
Distance Matrix for Google Maps API

questions.explanation: For precise time estimates in auto-routing and auto-dispatch, you must set the Private Key and Client ID for Google Maps API in system properties. These credentials authenticate requests to the Google Maps Distance Matrix API which calculates accurate travel time and distance between locations, replacing less precise straight-line estimates.

questions.stem: When configuring dynamic scheduling, what can you use or create to identify specific lists of tasks?
questions.explanation: Task filters in dynamic scheduling allow you to define criteria for identifying specific lists of tasks. Each filter has conditions that specify which tasks to include, resource type settings, and auto assignment configuration. Task filters are the primary mechanism for organizing tasks into groups for dynamic scheduling assignment.

questions.stem: As it pertains to dynamic scheduling system properties, what is the recommended maximum number of tasks that can be selected when running dynamic scheduling manually?
questions.explanation: The recommended maximum number of tasks that can be selected when running dynamic scheduling manually is 50, as defined in the dynamic scheduling system properties. Selecting more tasks increases processing time and may impact scheduling quality. This limit balances scheduling accuracy with system performance for manual scheduling operations.

questions.stem: What does dynamic scheduling use to stack rank each field agent to determine the best agent for routing?
questions.explanation: Dynamic scheduling uses the Ranking method to stack rank each field agent to determine the best agent for routing. The ranking method defines how agents are scored based on weighted matching criteria (like skills match, proximity, availability). Agents are ranked from best to worst fit using the formula: (Criteria_rating x Criteria_weight) / total_weight for each criterion, producing a final ranking score.

questions.stem: What scheduled job considers the tasks assigned to or accepted by agents on the current date and automatically enhances the routes for those tasks?
questions.explanation: The "Optimize Task Routing" scheduled job runs daily at 3:00 AM system time. It considers tasks assigned to or accepted by agents on the current date and automatically enhances their routes to minimize travel time. This is the standard scheduled job for automatic route optimization in FSM.

questions.stem: As it pertains to scheduling, what considers time between tasks, task dependencies, toll roads, and other specified time buffers?
questions.explanation: Route Optimization considers time between tasks, task dependencies, toll roads, and other specified time buffers when scheduling. It goes beyond basic scheduling by calculating optimal travel routes that account for real-world factors like road conditions, toll costs, travel time between consecutive tasks, and required buffer time. The Dispatcher Workspace (A) and Dynamic Scheduling (B) use route optimization data but don't perform these calculations themselves.

questions.stem: As it pertains to dynamic scheduling configuration, what are the main components of task filters? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The main components of task filters in dynamic scheduling configuration are: (A) Weighting — assigns relative importance to each criterion, (B) Matching criteria — defines what agent attributes are evaluated against task requirements, and (E) Ranking method — determines how matched agents are scored and ordered. Un-assignment constraints (C) and ordering rules (D) are separate dynamic scheduling components, not part of task filters.

questions.stem: What is the recommended maximum number of tasks that can be selected when running dynamic scheduling manually?
questions.explanation: The recommended maximum number of tasks when running dynamic scheduling manually is 50. This system property limit ensures the scheduling engine can process tasks efficiently without degrading performance. Selecting too many tasks at once (75 or 100) increases computation time exponentially as the engine must evaluate all possible agent-task combinations.

questions.stem: Where can you control the maximum number of tasks that can be selected when manually running dynamic scheduling?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of tasks that can be selected when manually running dynamic scheduling is controlled via Dynamic scheduling system properties. System properties provide global configuration settings including task selection limits for manual scheduling operations. The dynamic scheduling configuration defines filters and criteria, not task count limits.

questions.stem: As it pertains to dynamic scheduling, what is this an example of government customers are higher rank and private sector customers are lower?
questions.explanation: The example of government customers being higher rank and private sector customers being lower is a Task ordering rule. Task ordering rules define the sequence in which tasks are processed by dynamic scheduling based on business priorities. By ranking government customers higher, their tasks are scheduled first, ensuring priority service. This differs from task filters (which select tasks) and matching criteria (which evaluate agents).

questions.stem: Which operational role is responsible for reviewing reports, metrics, and team performance?
questions.explanation: The wm_manager operational role is responsible for reviewing reports, metrics, and team performance. FSM managers focus on operational oversight — monitoring KPIs like first-time fix rates, SLA compliance, and agent utilization. They use dashboards and reports to identify trends, address performance issues, and make strategic decisions about resource allocation and process improvements.

questions.stem: Which operational role is responsible for scheduling appointments and assigning tasks to agents?
questions.explanation: The wm_dispatcher operational role is responsible for scheduling appointments and assigning tasks to agents. Dispatchers use the dispatcher workspace to view agent calendars, manage task queues, manually assign or reassign tasks, and coordinate the daily schedule. They serve as the bridge between incoming work orders and field agents, ensuring optimal task distribution.

questions.stem: As it pertains to the Agent Feedback feature, ServiceNow calculates the average rating of a field agent and stores it in which table?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow calculates the average rating of a field agent from the Agent Feedback feature and stores it in the wm_agent_rating table. This table aggregates customer feedback scores into an average rating per agent, which can be used in reports, dashboards, and potentially as input to dynamic scheduling ranking criteria to factor agent quality into task assignments.

questions.stem: As it pertains to dynamic scheduling configuration, if you are ranking agents based on the number of parts available in the agent stockroom, which matching criterion should you configure in the task filters?

options.text: Matching Mandatory Parts for Dynamic Scheduling
Matching Agents With Most Parts For Dynamic Scheduling
Matching Skill Level Gap for Dynamic Scheduling

questions.explanation: "Matching Agents With Most Parts For Dynamic Scheduling" (documented as "Agents with most parts") is the matching criterion for ranking agents based on the number of available parts in their stockroom. It's a scripted criterion that identifies agents with the most required parts for a task. Matching Mandatory Parts only checks mandatory parts, and the Skills criteria are unrelated to parts.

questions.stem: Which operational role can view the calendars of team members to check availability, view the skill distribution, and create or edit skills of team members?
questions.explanation: The wm_qualifier operational role can view calendars of team members to check availability, view skill distribution, and create or edit skills of team members. Qualifiers are responsible for managing the technical qualifications and skills of the field workforce, ensuring agents are properly certified and that skills data is accurate for dynamic scheduling decisions.

questions.stem: What controls the visibility of the ‘Optimize route’ option in the more actions menu in the agent card on dispatcher workspace?
questions.explanation: The system property sn_fsm_disp_wrkspc.enable_optimize_route controls the visibility of the "Optimize route" option in the more actions menu on the agent card in Dispatcher Workspace. Setting it to true enables the route optimization option. UI actions, client scripts, and business rules do not control this specific visibility.

questions.stem: What can customers use on the service portal to view and select available service windows?
questions.explanation: Customers can use the Appointment booking feature on the service portal to view and select available service windows. This self-service capability shows customers the available time slots based on agent availability and scheduling rules, allowing them to pick a convenient window for their field service visit. It improves customer experience by giving them control over scheduling.

questions.stem: What do you need to configure an appointment booking service? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: To configure an appointment booking service, you need: (B) a record producer to create the service request, (C) an appointment booking variable set to display available time slots and capture the customer's selection, and (D) a work order template to define the type of work being scheduled. Contextual search (A), recipients list (E), and publication article (F) are unrelated to appointment booking setup.

questions.stem: Assuming task-driven process lifecycle is enabled, how many work order tasks are required for a work order request?
questions.explanation: When task-driven process lifecycle is enabled, at least one work order task is required for a work order request. The task-driven lifecycle means the work order's state progression is driven by its child tasks — the work order cannot advance through its lifecycle stages without at least one task to drive the process. This enforces proper work breakdown and task tracking.

questions.stem: How do you prevent a task which has been rejected by an agent from being dynamically assigned to the same agent in the next 24 hours?

options.text: Configure the rejected technician duration system property
Configure unassignment constraints for dynamic scheduling

questions.explanation: To prevent a rejected task from being dynamically assigned to the same agent in the next 24 hours, configure the rejected technician duration system property (work.management.rejected.technician.duration). The "Ignore Rejected Technician" matching criterion reads this property to exclude recently-rejecting agents during the specified period.

questions.stem: Users can be assigned work order tasks and edit these records if they: (Choose two.)

options.text: Belong to the Dispatch Group the task is assigned to
Belong to the Assignment Group the task is assigned to

questions.explanation: Users can be assigned work order tasks and edit records if they have the wm_agent role (C) which grants agent permissions for FSM tasks, AND belong to the Assignment Group the task is assigned to (D) which determines task access. The Dispatch Group is for dispatchers not agents, and wm_edit is not a standard FSM role.

questions.stem: How are dispatch groups filtered in the lookup?
questions.explanation: Dispatch groups are filtered in the lookup by Location coverage. When dispatchers select a dispatch group, the lookup filters available groups based on the location coverage areas they serve. This ensures dispatchers only see groups that are relevant to the geographic area of the work order, preventing assignment to groups that don't serve that location.

questions.stem: Dependencies can only be set for work order tasks in which state?
questions.explanation: Dependencies can only be set for work order tasks in Draft state. Tasks are created in Draft state where they can be fully configured including dependency relationships. Once tasks are promoted from Draft to Pending Dispatch, their dependency configuration is locked. The t_PromoteDraftWorkOrderTasks process advances tasks from Draft.

questions.stem: If geolocation is not enabled, the agent’s starting position for a given day defaults to what?

options.text: The last task location for each field agent for a given day
The first task location for each field agent for a given day
The geographic coordinates returned from the agent’s mobile device

questions.explanation: When geolocation is not enabled, the agent's starting position for a given day defaults to the first task location. Without real-time GPS data from the mobile device, the system uses the first scheduled task's location as a proxy for the agent's starting position when calculating travel times and optimizing routes.

questions.stem: Which of the following resources are critical for a successful implementation? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: Five critical resources for a successful FSM implementation: (C) Field service manager for process design and operational leadership, (E) Field service agent for UAT and workflow validation, (F) System Administrator for technical configuration, (G) Dispatcher for scheduling process design, and (H) Qualifier for skills and qualification framework setup. CEO and CIO provide sponsorship but aren't hands-on implementation resources.

questions.stem: Which operational role is responsible for managing field agent skills?
questions.explanation: The wm_qualifier operational role is responsible for managing field agent skills. Qualifiers maintain the skills database, assign skills to agents, verify certifications, and ensure agents' skill profiles are accurate and up-to-date. This is critical for dynamic scheduling, which relies on accurate skill data to match the right agents to tasks requiring specific competencies.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of Intraday Schedule Optimization?

options.text: To plan tasks for the entire week
To consider tasks that were scheduled previously
To re-optimize schedules in real-time based on changing conditions

questions.stem: What is the purpose of intraday schedule optimization?

options.text: To manage an agents’ travel time
To update agent schedules as new events occur throughout the day

questions.stem: What actions can an agent perform when removing a part from a task? (Choose two.)

options.text: Donate the part to a local warehouse
Set the asset status to available, but defective

questions.explanation: When removing a part from a task, an agent can: set the part as defective (B) to flag it for repair or disposal, or replace the part (E) by substituting it with a different part. Donating to a warehouse (A), throwing away (C), and marking as "available but defective" (D) are not standard FSM part removal actions.

questions.stem: Where can users control the maximum number of tasks that can be selected when manually running dynamic scheduling?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of tasks that can be selected when manually running dynamic scheduling is controlled via Dynamic Scheduling System Properties. These system properties configure global parameters for the dynamic scheduling engine including selection limits, batch sizes, and scheduling behavior.

What factors does intraday schedule automation consider? (Choose three.)

options.text: Whether the agent is running early or late
Number of tasks scheduled for tomorrow

questions.explanation: Intraday schedule automation considers three factors: time of day (B) to assess current schedule position, number of incomplete tasks pending (C) to evaluate remaining workload, and whether the agent is running early or late (D) to trigger schedule adjustments. Tasks completed yesterday (A) and tasks scheduled for tomorrow (E) are not relevant to intraday optimization.
